text: What is the main purpose of preparing Receipts and Payments Account?
options: To find out the surplus or deficit at the end of the year
To prepare the Balance Sheet at the end of the year
To show the inflows and outflows of cash and bank during the year
To calculate the net profit or loss of the organization
explanation: Receipts and Payments Account is a cash-based account that records all the inflows and outflows of cash and bank during the year. It helps in identifying the cash transactions of the organization.
subject: Accountancy

text: Which of the following is not a feature of Receipts and Payments Account?
options: It is a cash-based account
It is a nominal account
It is prepared at the end of the year
It is a real account
explanation: Receipts and Payments Account is a real account as it deals with the actual inflows and outflows of cash and bank. It is not a nominal account as it does not appear in the Balance Sheet.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the purpose of preparing Income and Expenditure Account?
options: To find out the surplus or deficit at the end of the year
To prepare the Balance Sheet at the end of the year
To show the inflows and outflows of cash and bank during the year
To calculate the net profit or loss of the organization
explanation: Income and Expenditure Account is an accrual-based account that records all the inflows and outflows of income and expenditure during the year. It helps in calculating the net profit or loss of the organization.
subject: Accountancy

text: Which of the following is not a feature of Income and Expenditure Account?
options: It is an accrual-based account
It is a nominal account
It is prepared at the end of the year
It is a real account
explanation: Income and Expenditure Account is a nominal account as it appears in the Balance Sheet. It is not a real account as it deals with the inflows and outflows of income and expenditure, not actual cash transactions.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the purpose of subscription adjustments?
options: To find out the surplus or deficit at the end of the year
To prepare the Balance Sheet at the end of the year
To show the inflows and outflows of cash and bank during the year
To adjust the subscriptions received in advance or in arrears
explanation: Subscription adjustments are made to adjust the subscriptions received in advance or in arrears. This helps in matching the subscriptions with the expenses incurred during the year.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the effect of legacy on the Receipts and Payments Account?
options: It is treated as a receipt
It is treated as an expenditure
It is treated as a capital receipt
It is treated as a revenue receipt
explanation: Legacy is treated as a capital receipt in the Receipts and Payments Account. It is a non-recurring receipt that is not related to the current year's activities.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the effect of legacy on the Income and Expenditure Account?
options: It is treated as a receipt
It is treated as an expenditure
It is treated as a capital receipt
It is treated as a revenue receipt
explanation: Legacy is treated as a capital receipt in the Income and Expenditure Account. It is a non-recurring receipt that is not related to the current year's activities.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the purpose of specific funds?
options: To find out the surplus or deficit at the end of the year
To prepare the Balance Sheet at the end of the year
To show the inflows and outflows of cash and bank during the year
To earmark funds for specific purposes
explanation: Specific funds are earmarked funds that are set aside for specific purposes. This helps in ensuring that the funds are used for the intended purpose.
subject: Accountancy

text: How is the Balance Sheet prepared for a not-for-profit organization?
options: By preparing the Receipts and Payments Account and the Income and Expenditure Account
By preparing the Balance Sheet at the end of the year
By preparing the Balance Sheet at the beginning of the year
By preparing the Balance Sheet for a specific period
explanation: The Balance Sheet for a not-for-profit organization is prepared by preparing the Receipts and Payments Account and the Income and Expenditure Account. This helps in identifying the assets, liabilities, and capital of the organization.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the difference between the Receipts and Payments Account and the Income and Expenditure Account?
options: Receipts and Payments Account is a real account, while Income and Expenditure Account is a nominal account
Receipts and Payments Account is an accrual-based account, while Income and Expenditure Account is a cash-based account
Receipts and Payments Account is prepared at the end of the year, while Income and Expenditure Account is prepared at the beginning of the year
Receipts and Payments Account is prepared for a specific period, while Income and Expenditure Account is prepared for the entire year
explanation: Receipts and Payments Account is a real account that deals with the actual inflows and outflows of cash and bank, while Income and Expenditure Account is a nominal account that deals with the inflows and outflows of income and expenditure.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the purpose of adjusting the subscriptions received in advance?
options: To find out the surplus or deficit at the end of the year
To prepare the Balance Sheet at the end of the year
To show the inflows and outflows of cash and bank during the year
To adjust the subscriptions received in advance or in arrears
explanation: Adjusting the subscriptions received in advance helps in matching the subscriptions with the expenses incurred during the year. This ensures that the subscriptions are used for the intended purpose.
subject: Accountancy
